 NRS Gives Crypto Operators November 30 Deadline for Tax Registration
 November 20, 2026 0 122 
 Share on Facebook 
 Tweet on Twitter 
 Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) (formerly FIRS) 
 The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has given cryptocurrency operators and other virtual asset service providers (VASPs) operating in Nigeria until November 30, 2026, to register on its newly introduced Virtual Asset Service Provider Tax Portal. 
 The agency also directed affected individuals and businesses to complete their integration with the platform by December 31, 2026, warning that failure to comply with the stipulated deadlines could attract penalties and other enforcement measures under relevant laws.
 The directive was contained in a public notice titled Virtual Asset Service Providers Compliance Registration, published by the NRS on its official X handle on Friday.
 According to the agency, the initiative is designed to strengthen tax compliance, improve regulatory oversight and facilitate registration for anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and counter-proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF) purposes.
 The NRS explained that individuals and businesses involved in virtual asset activities are subject to existing tax obligations, including registration, proper record-keeping, reporting and payment of applicable taxes.
 It said the portal was deployed pursuant to Section 71 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, which provides for the use of technology to automate tax administration processes.
 The platform is also intended to support the registration of virtual asset service providers in line with the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendation 15.
 The agency stated that the directive covers all persons providing virtual asset services in Nigeria or to individuals resident in the country, irrespective of whether the service providers maintain a physical presence in Nigeria.
 Covered activities include cryptocurrency-to-naira and other fiat currency exchanges, transactions between different virtual assets, digital asset transfers, custody and administration of virtual assets, as well as the operation of cryptocurrency exchanges and trading platforms.
 Other affected activities include digital asset-based payment, settlement, remittance and money transfer services, alongside the issuance, distribution and redemption of virtual assets.
 The requirements also extend to staking, lending, borrowing and other financial services involving digital assets.
 However, the NRS clarified that the introduction of the portal does not create new taxes or additional tax obligations for operators, stressing that it is a technology-driven platform for administering existing obligations.
 It further warned that the phased implementation of the portal does not suspend or exempt virtual asset operators from complying with tax requirements already established under Nigerian law.
 The agency also emphasised that registration on the platform does not automatically grant a licence or authorisation to operate a virtual asset business in Nigeria.
 It urged all affected individuals and businesses to complete their registration before November 30 and conclude the required integration by December 31, 2026, to avoid possible sanctions.
 Registration is available through the NRS Virtual Asset Service Provider Tax Portal: [https://vasp.nrs.gov.ng/](https://vasp.nrs.gov.ng/?utm_source=chatgpt.com).
